core_concept: Accelerates vector nearest-neighbor search by subdividing coarse clusters and using triangle-inequality distance bounds to losslessly prune non-candidate vectors without computing high-dimensional distances.

technical_novelty: Unlike standard inverted-file (IVF) indexes that evaluate all vectors within selected centroids, this architecture implements fine-grained secondary cluster subdivision paired with scalar distance caching to evaluate triangle inequality bounds |d(q, c) - d(x, c)| <= d(q, x), skipping over 99% of exact floating-point vector dot products.

summary: TriMetric builds a high-granularity cluster-based indexing engine that solves the coarse-granularity scanning overhead in vector retrieval. This project serves as an exceptional systems and algorithms portfolio capstone bridging metric data structures and modern vector database systems.
core_mechanism: Hierarchical metric clustering combined with Triangle Inequality Pruning: for query q, sub-centroid c, candidate vector x, and current k-th nearest neighbor radius R, vectors are skipped without distance evaluation whenever |d(q, c) - d(x, c)| > R.
